verdict.rationale: LaunchDarkly's docs say experiments can use data from an external warehouse such as Snowflake. Numeric metrics are built from custom events the customer sends, so metrics can come from the user's own warehouse or ingested events. The evidence is one-line mentions only: there is no detail on defining metrics directly from warehouse tables (SQL or table mapping), which warehouses are supported, or how events are ingested, so complete coverage is not shown. missing for 10: documented workflow for defining metrics from warehouse tables, breadth of supported warehouses, detail on custom-event metric definition, independent or hands-on corroboration

support.subject: As a product manager, I can define experiment metrics from my own data — warehouse tables or ingested events — instead of a black-box metric store

citations.quote: You can also run experiments using data from an external warehouse, like Snowflake.
You must use custom events to create numeric metrics, which measure and analyze numerical values against a baseline that you set.
You can measure things like page views, clicks, load time, infrastructure costs, and more.
